quiz.q: What globally significant animal is found only in Morocco and Algeria in the wild?
options: The Moroccan lion — a subspecies found only in the Atlas Mountains
The Barbary macaque — the only wild primate in Africa north of the Sahara, and the only wild macaque outside Asia — lives only in Morocco and Algeria
The Barbary leopard is unique to Morocco — Algeria has no leopards
The Fennec fox is found only in Morocco — all other wild populations are in captivity
quiz.explanation: The Barbary macaque (Macaca sylvanus) is the only wild primate in Africa north of the Sahara, and the only wild macaque found outside Asia. Its wild range is restricted to Morocco and Algeria (the Atlas and Rif Mountains). Morocco has the largest population — approximately 5,000-6,000 individuals. The species is endangered: habitat loss (cedar forest clearing), illegal collection for tourist photo opportunities, and climate change are threatening the population. The Barbary macaque is also the famous 'Rock Ape' of Gibraltar (a small population was introduced there centuries ago). Its restricted range makes Moroccan and Algerian forest conservation critical for global primate biodiversity.

laws.title: Morocco Digital Economy Strategy
laws.subtitle: Morocco's digital transformation and tech sector growth
laws.fullDescription: Morocco's Digital Morocco 2030 strategy aims to position Morocco as Africa's digital hub. Morocco has relative tech advantages: skilled French-educated workforce, proximity to Europe, undersea cable connections to Europe and West Africa, and competitive costs. Casablanca Technopark and Rabat's Technopolis host tech companies and startups. Morocco is a significant call center and business process outsourcing (BPO) destination for French-speaking Europe. The fintech sector is growing: mobile money (Orange Money, Inwi Money) reaching the unbanked population. Morocco launched a 5G spectrum auction. Digital challenges: digital divide between urban and rural Morocco, digital literacy gaps, and the concentration of tech talent in Casablanca and Rabat.
laws.penalty: Electronic fraud: up to 5 years imprisonment. Unauthorized data processing: CNDP (Data Protection Commission) penalties. Cybercrime: up to 10 years for serious offenses.
exceptions: Academic digital research has modified data access protections
E-government services have simplified digital identity requirements for citizens
Tech companies in Casablanca Finance City have modified data transfer regulations

quiz.q: Why is Morocco attractive for French companies looking to set up call centers and BPO operations?
options: Morocco has the cheapest internet in the world — making digital operations cost-free

French-educated skilled workforce, proximity to France (short time zone difference), competitive labor costs, and cultural/linguistic alignment make Morocco ideal for French-language business process outsourcing
Morocco offers complete tax exemption for any French company — an unmatched incentive
Morocco's government guarantees all French business investments with sovereign guarantee
quiz.explanation: Morocco is one of Europe's — specifically France's — top near-shoring BPO destinations: Moroccan workers are French-educated (French is Morocco's language of business and higher education despite Arabic/Amazigh being official), time zone difference is just 1-2 hours, labor costs are 3-4x cheaper than France, and cultural familiarity is high (Morocco was French protectorate until 1956). Major French companies (Orange, Total, Société Générale) have significant Moroccan BPO operations. Casablanca is sometimes called 'the 22nd French region' in business circles due to its French corporate presence.

laws.title: Moroccan Traditional Medicine Law and Herb Markets
laws.subtitle: Traditional herbal medicine integration in Morocco
laws.fullDescription: Morocco has a rich traditional medicine tradition: Amazigh, Arab, and sub-Saharan African healing practices using herbs, minerals, and animal products. Moroccan herb markets (souks des herboristeries) in Marrakech, Fes, and other cities sell hundreds of plants. Morocco has 4,200+ medicinal plant species. Traditional healers (tbibs, sherifa, fqih) operate alongside formal medical system. Morocco legalized herbal medicine practitioners (herboristes) under a separate regulatory framework. Moroccan argan oil — from the Argan tree found only in southwestern Morocco — has become a global luxury product ($1B+ export industry). Moroccan rose water, ras el hanout spice blends, and Black Seed (Nigella sativa) are significant traditional and commercial products.
laws.penalty: Practicing medicine without license (non-herbalist): up to 2 years. Selling dangerous herbal products: administrative confiscation. Fraud on herbal product labeling: administrative and criminal penalties.
exceptions: Licensed herboristerie graduates may sell and recommend herbal products without medical license
Religious healer (fqih) spiritual services that do not include herbal prescriptions have no formal regulation
Cosmetic use of argan, rose, and other plant products operates under cosmetics regulatory framework only

quiz.q: What is unique about Morocco's Argan tree and why is argan oil a premium export product?
options: The Argan tree is found only in Morocco — nowhere else on earth — making its oil an inherently unique Moroccan product worth $1B+ in annual exports
Argan trees grow throughout North Africa and the Middle East — Morocco just markets them better
Argan oil is valuable because it is the primary ingredient in Moroccan food, not cosmetics
The Argan tree is extinct in the wild — only cultivated specimens exist
quiz.explanation: The Argan tree (Argania spinosa) grows naturally only in southwestern Morocco (and a very small area in Algeria) — it is literally found nowhere else on Earth. This geographic exclusivity makes Argan oil inherently a Moroccan product. The oil — extracted from Argan nuts by Berber women cooperatives — is valued for culinary use and, especially, for hair and skin cosmetics. The cosmetics industry drove an explosion in demand: major international beauty brands use Argan oil as a premium ingredient. Morocco exports $1B+ of Argan oil annually, much of it through women-run cooperatives that have become economic development models.

laws.title: Morocco Terrorism Law and Islamist Groups
laws.subtitle: Morocco's counter-terrorism record after Casablanca bombings
laws.fullDescription: Morocco's counter-terrorism framework strengthened dramatically after the 2003 Casablanca bombings (12 suicide bombers killed 45 people including themselves). Morocco enacted Anti-Terrorism Law 03-03 creating: terrorism offenses, special courts, and expanded surveillance powers. Morocco has been largely successful at preventing major attacks since 2003: active intelligence cooperation with France, Spain, and US; penetration of domestic networks; and deradicalization program (Moussalaha). The Marrakech Café Argana bombing (2011, 17 killed) was the most significant post-2003 attack. ISIS recruited Moroccan fighters for Syria (1,500-2,000 estimated): returning fighters represent a security challenge. The 2018 murders of two Scandinavian tourists in the High Atlas were ISIS-inspired.
laws.penalty: Terrorist act causing death: life imprisonment to death penalty. Financing terrorism: up to 20 years. Recruiting for terrorist organization: up to 30 years. Joining foreign terrorist group: up to 20 years.
exceptions: Deradicalization program (Moussalaha) participants cooperating with authorities receive reduced sentences
Reporting planned terrorist activity: protected informant status available
Religious education in approved institutions protected — counter-extremism outreach is encouraged

quiz.q: What 2003 event transformed Morocco's counter-terrorism approach?
options: Morocco never experienced terrorism — it adopted counter-terrorism laws preemptively

The 2003 Casablanca bombings (12 suicide bombers, 45 killed) led to new anti-terrorism law, special courts, and intelligence reforms that made Morocco relatively successful at preventing subsequent attacks
Morocco adopted counter-terrorism laws after joining the US-led coalition in Afghanistan
The 2003 US invasion of Iraq prompted Morocco to preemptively adopt counter-terrorism measures
quiz.explanation: The May 2003 Casablanca bombings — 12 coordinated suicide attacks by Moroccan Islamist group Salafiya Jihadiya, killing 45 people at Spanish and Jewish targets — were Morocco's deadliest terrorist attack. The attacks forced Morocco to fundamentally reform counter-terrorism: Law 03-03 created specific terrorism offenses, special courts for terrorism cases, expanded intelligence powers, and cooperation with Western intelligence services expanded. Morocco subsequently built a reputation for effective counter-terrorism, sharing intelligence that prevented European attacks. The deradicalization program (Moussalaha) combining religion, psychology, and community support has been studied internationally.

laws.title: Tanger-Med Port and Morocco's Trade Infrastructure
laws.subtitle: Africa's largest container port and Morocco's logistics ambition
laws.fullDescription: Tanger-Med port complex (opened 2007, expanded 2021) is Africa's largest container port: 9M TEU capacity, ranked among world's top 20. Tanger-Med transformed Morocco's trade logistics: automotive exports from Renault and PSA factories, re-export hub for sub-Saharan Africa, and container transshipment (routing containers between large and small ships). Tanger-Med includes a free zone (TFZ, with 1,000+ companies) and passenger ferry terminal. The port has attracted €10B+ in investment. Morocco's logistics strategy: Tanger-Med as a gateway for Africa trade, competing with Algeciras (Spain) across the Strait of Gibraltar for Mediterranean transshipment. The port is seen as Morocco's economic anchor for the northern region.
laws.penalty: Port violations: maritime authority penalties. Smuggling through free zone: criminal prosecution. Port security violations: criminal prosecution with potential terrorism charges.
exceptions: TFZ free zone companies have modified customs and tax regulations
Transit cargo is exempt from Moroccan import duties
Maritime repair and provisioning are exempt from certain port fees

quiz.q: What is Tanger-Med's strategic significance for Morocco and African trade?
options: Tanger-Med handles only cruise ships — not container trade

Africa's largest container port (9M TEU capacity) has transformed Morocco into a regional logistics hub, competing with Spanish Algeciras across the Strait of Gibraltar for Mediterranean transshipment traffic
Tanger-Med is primarily a fishing port — containers are a minor activity
Tanger-Med is closed to African trade — it only serves European-Moroccan trade
quiz.explanation: Tanger-Med — located at the strategic chokepoint where Mediterranean meets Atlantic, just 14km from Spain — has become Africa's largest container port. Its 9M TEU capacity handles Morocco's exports (especially automotive — Renault and Stellantis vehicles), trans-Atlantic container transshipment (repositioning containers from large oceanic vessels to smaller feeder ships), and re-export cargo for West Africa. The port competes directly with Algeciras (Spain) across the Strait — Morocco vs. Spain for Mediterranean hub port status. Tanger-Med represents Morocco's transformation from agricultural/phosphate exporter to a logistics and manufacturing gateway economy.
